ideas.title: Sled the cart down the dune: plough to brake, lean to steer, tip if you lean wrong
ideas.goal: Push the empty cart to the dune top, three friends pile in, let go. It runs downhill by gravity; the player brakes by driving a stick into the sand (deeper = more drag, but it can snag and slew the cart round) and steers by calling the friends to lean: their weight sinks one side's wheels deeper and the cart turns towards them, and on a side slope too much lean rolls it over and spills them into the sand. Reaching the water without stopping or tipping is the run; the ruts and berms of every run stay and change the next one, and after rain or near the water the same dune runs differently.
ideas.toward: The cart's rolling resistance, load transfer and rollover on the real dune, before the motor goes on; the friends ride along as at the big goal's end.
ideas.idea: Nothing typed per dune: the cart is a PrintSim affine body (mass and inertia from its parts, the friends' bodies as masses at their real seat positions, moving as they lean), wheels and stick touch the SandField through ONE soil-tool model: Bekker-Wong sinkage and Janosi shear for wheels, McKyes/Reece passive pressure for any blade (stick, beak, plank edge). The soil's cohesion, friction angle and density come from the sand field's own state per cell: moisture (distance to water, rain), compaction from earlier passes (old ruts are firmer), using Wong's measured values for dry and moist sand; a check script reproduces published Reece blade-force and Wong sinkage measurements before it is used. Rollover is the rigid body's own: it tips when the resultant of gravity and the wheels' reactions leaves the wheel track. The friends hold on with poses solved from the cart's acceleration (they lurch, grab, get thrown on a tip). Watching: three ponies shrieking downhill, a plume of sand off the stick, the cart slewing and rolling.
ideas.form: physics/soiltool.jl (with its check against the published measurements) + a Jump in ride on the dune built on the cart; R digging switches to the same model; a traced 10 s short from the dune's foot.

ideas.title: Work any metal cold, and what you made decides how the part works
ideas.goal: Lumi lays metal on the flat rock and the player strikes it with a hand stone, where and how hard: lead squashes into a sheet, copper work-hardens and gets springy until annealed in the fire, an iron nail barely dents. What you made is not a trophy: a lead sheet's thin spots corrode through first in the cell (it dies where you hammered it thin), its area decides how much current it can give; a copper brush hammered springy presses on the commutator and sparks less than a soft one that sags. Making a better part is the skill, and you see why when the cart runs.
ideas.toward: Plates for the accumulator and brushes and segments for the motor, made by hand, with their quality carried into how the cart drives.
ideas.idea: J2 plasticity with isotropic hardening in PrintSim's FEM for every metal, from each metal's measured yield stress, hardening curve and recrystallisation temperature (lead never hardens at room temperature, copper does until annealed), the blow a real contact impulse from the stone's mass and speed. The resulting thickness and hardness fields are kept with the part and read by the cell (corrosion per patch, area) and the motor (brush spring force from the hardened strip's stiffness). Watching: a grey foot squashing into a sheet with toe-shaped lobes; a copper strip that suddenly springs back.
ideas.form: A material model in dev/PrintSim used by every metal on the island + a hammering spot at the cove rock in Jump in; the parts carry their fields into the cell and motor plugins.
